title: 10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10)
summary: For his 10-year gym anniversary, NH shows an upper/arm day (backpack ring push-ups with rest-pause, belt rows for traps, pinwheel curls, front raises, weighted ab-wheel rollouts) and a lower day (heels-elevated squats, snatch-grip hyperextensions, calves). He then reveals his nightly rice-bucket forearm routine. He is at 220 lb and recomping, and insists that 10 honest natural years should leave anyone jacked.
claims: Anyone who has truly put in 10 years natural will end up jacked; if not, they did something wrong, and being natural isn't the reason
Warm-ups matter but need only 1-2 sets to get the tendons ready for heavy sets
Wrap the pinwheel-curl strap around the hand, not the thumb, to tax the pronators less and work the brachioradialis more
Doing ring push-ups in an incline stance gives a better lower-chest stretch and lets him use more weight
Rest-pause properly: go to failure, rest 10-15 seconds, then continue; he usually gets 2-3 more reps of high-stimulus 'free volume'
Rest-pause is taxing; start with only 1-2 rest-pause sets
At 220 lb and high body fat he is recomping while he still progresses, and will resume the bulk afterwards
For traps he does belt rows: heavy for 10 reps, stretching at the bottom and pulling with the whole upper back, without caring much about elbow height
With a narrow build he leans into his strong points; a V-taper is hard for him, so he chases a Bizu-style physique with huge traps
Without straps he'd lose 20-30% performance; using straps whenever grip fails can multiply upper-back gains
If a movement hurts your tendons, drop it; there are always pain-free alternatives
He swapped a painful handle finger curl for fat-grip gooseneck reverse curls
On pinwheel curls let the weight stretch the arm but never fully lock the elbow; the angle protects the biceps tendon, so he can push hard
Rest-pause breaks plateaus on isolation lifts; it lets him add 2 lb a session instead of being stuck at 50 lb
Bring in rest-pause first on isolations, then upper-body compounds, and only later on lower-body compounds
Reps after the pause must be the hardest of the set; if they are easier you are doing rest-pause wrong
Brachioradialis work, such as pinwheel curls or hammer curls on a preacher, gives wider-looking arms from the front
Dumbbell front raises with an upper-chest flex before lifting train the front delts and upper chest; do 10-15 reps without cheating
Rotating the wrist inward at the top of a front raise, like turning the fist into a hook, reduces shoulder stress and shifts work to the upper chest
Front-delt isolation is worthwhile 'free volume' even though presses train the front delts
If you don't enjoy training a muscle you won't grow it
A bulk is the best time to train abs: they grow most in a surplus, and it limits the bulk's hit to your aesthetics
Do weighted ab-wheel rollouts slowly and stay stretched at the bottom; rushing risks the shoulders
Steeply heels-elevated squats let him keep upright, quad-biased form that would be impossible flat-footed; only the speed changes near failure, never the form
Snatch-grip hyperextensions holding 25-lb plates rather than 45s give more range and a hamstring bias; elevate the bench to bias the lower back
Back thickness and lower-back detail come from heavy hip hinges, not just rows and pulldowns
Long tibias and long calf insertions make his 16-17 inch calves look like 13 inches; complaining or blaming genetics is useless, so keep training them
For two months he has done 20-30 minutes of rice-bucket training every night, using a spoon to make it harder
Rice-bucket training is mainly for forearm conditioning and wrist health, not size
His big forearms come from years of forearm isolation, not genetics or rice buckets; any body part grows with a method and discipline
Rubber-band finger extensions complete rice-bucket work and help finger, arm and elbow health
exercises: backpack load, ring to armpit, rest-pause
strap around hand not thumb, elbow never fully locked, rest-pause
heavy 10 reps, stretch at bottom, straps
shrug and flex upper chest first, rotate wrist inward at top, 10-15 reps
steep angle, knees tracking, same form every rep
25-lb plates for range, plate touches floor
hamstrings; elevate bench to bias lower back
